# Ribbon Planning Tab

## How To Build

A RibbonPlanningTab should be built as a reusable component that will be reused throughout the rest of the codebase.  A component is configurable through arguments or properties that alter its behaviour, appearance, and details.  A RibbonPlanningTab should encapsulate all of its own reusable behaviour, while leaving the wiring, integration, and integration to the domain of the application.

## Theme

Drawn in the [Theme](../../../theme/index.md#theme): its surfaces, text, lines, accent, and status colours are the theme's roles, named as the theme names them, in both dark and light mode, never colours of its own.

## Pitch

The ribbon's Planning tab: the commands for planning work before it is sent, as the [Planning](../../../../scope/planning/index.md#planning) says.

## Description

The Planning tab of the ribbon, between Project and Code. It takes no mode's colour: its label is in the tab row's own colour, as Project's and Application's are.

## Groups

A "Plan" group holds the Open Planning command, then New Story, then Send Sprint. An "Agent" group follows it, holding Draft Stories, then Research.

## Commands

```
openPlanning: A "Planning" button with a checklist icon. Clicking it opens the Planning tab in the body, or selects it where it is open. Its tooltip says it opens the project's stories and sprint.
  It is primary, and a full button.
newStory: A "New Story" button with a plus icon. Clicking it opens Planning and adds a story to Next sprint, its title focused.
  It is primary, and a slim button.
sendSprint: A "Send Sprint" button with a send icon, enabled while Next sprint holds a story not yet sent. Clicking it sends the sprint, as Planning's Send sprint does; its tooltip says how many stories it sends.
  It is a slim button, and not primary.
draftStories: A "Draft Stories" button with a sparkle icon. Clicking it opens Planning, or selects its tab where it is open, and opens drafting in the side panel with its "Describe what you want" box focused, exactly as the Backlog heading's "Draft stories" button and Ctrl+Shift+D do, by the same route, not a copy of it. Its tooltip says it asks the agent to break a request into proposed stories, and gives Ctrl+Shift+D (Cmd+Shift+D on macOS). It is never disabled while planning is paused, since drafting only changes the plan.
  It is a slim button, and not primary.
research: A "Research" button with a magnifying-glass icon. Clicking it opens Planning, or selects its tab where it is open, and opens research in the side panel with its "What should be looked into?" box focused, exactly as the Backlog heading's "Research" button and Ctrl+Shift+R do, by the same route, not a copy of it. Its tooltip says it asks the agent to look into a topic, read only, and gives Ctrl+Shift+R (Cmd+Shift+R on macOS). It is never disabled while planning is paused; a second research while paused keeps the pause, as Planning says.
  It is a slim button, and not primary.
```

## Creating

Creating a story is quick, as adding a card is in Trello and adding an issue is in Linear: a story is added in the list it belongs in, right where it will sit. The Backlog and Next sprint each end with an "Add story" line at their foot, beneath their last card, or beneath their empty state when they have none. Clicking it opens a composer in its place: a blank story card, drawn as the parts draw one, whose title is a text box, focused, in the mode last picked for a story, with nothing else to fill in. Typing a title and pressing Enter adds the story to that list, where the composer was, and opens another composer beneath it, so a list can be written down without the mouse. content.text:
I've added an "Agent" group to the ribbon's Planning tab, after "Plan". It holds two slim buttons that aren't primary, so the collapsed ribbon leaves them out: **Draft Stories** with a sparkle icon, then **Research** with a magnifying-glass icon. **I couldn't compile or run any of it**: this environment can't read `.suspense/system-prompts/`, which the build includes, and it wouldn't let me copy the crate elsewhere to check it.

- **One shared route:** `Planning` now has public `draft_stories` and `research` methods. The Backlog heading's buttons, Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+D and Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+R, and the ribbon buttons all go through these two methods, so the open-and-focus behaviour isn't copied anywhere.
- **What the ribbon buttons do:** each sends the same action the shortcut uses. The main window catches it and opens Planning, or selects its tab, then opens drafting or research in the side panel with its box focused. The main window's handlers are in `src/main_window.rs`, and the steps that open Planning and then the panel are in `src/prompt_mode.rs`.
- **Tooltips:** each says what the command does and shows its shortcut from the Planning key bindings, so macOS shows Cmd. To do this I made `planning::CONTEXT` visible to the rest of the crate.
- **Pause:** neither button is disabled while planning is paused. Both are disabled only when no project is open, like New Story.

The code matches the spec; I found no disagreement with the prompt. The working tree also has many uncommitted changes in other files from before this task; I left them alone.
